newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil power shares rose most in 1996 - report.
newsitem.headline: Brazil power shares rose most in 1996 - report.

text.p: Shares of Brazilian electrical energy companies, boosted by bright privatization prospects, posted the strongest gains in 1996, surpassing even strongly rising telecom stocks, a local newspaper said.
Gazeta Mercantil, citing figures from consultant Economatica, said power shares rose 102.2 percent in reais last year while telecommunications stocks climbed 101.2 percent.
The two sectors led the surge last year in the Sao Paulo bourse's Bovespa index of 49 most-traded, which climbed 67.7 percent in reais or 53.23 percent in dollars, it said.
Telecoms and power shares both benefitted in 1996 from tariff adjustments late in 1995, which boosted company profits, and the prospects for privatization, Gazeta said.
Power shares rose slightly more because the selloff process for power firms move forward more quickly, it added.

Shares of Sao Paulo state-owned Companhia Paulista de Forca e Luz (CPFL) climbed the most, rising a whopping 265 percent in reais in the year. It was followed Coelce and Eletropaulo, up 238 percent and 218 percent respectively.

The paper quoted analysts as saying that telecoms shares should make up ground against power shares this year after the auction of concessions to operate cellular telephone services on the B Band frequency.
